title: High-resolution Fiber-optic Microendoscopy for in situ Cellular Imaging
protocol: Connect the 6" cage rods to the 1.5" cage rods, forming a pair of 7.5" long rods.
Screw these rods into one face of the fold mirror unit.
Screw the 0.5" rods into the opposite face.
Slide the cage cube onto the cage rods via the two lower through holes.
Screw the 2" rods into the side face of the cage cube.
Attach the camera to a cage plate using a C-mount to SM1 adapter.
Secure the cage plate on the 0.5" cage rods, flush with the face of the fold mirror unit.
Insert the "tube" lens into a 3" long lens tube and secure it with a retaining ring.
Drop the emission filter into the tube on top of the first retaining ring and add another ring to secure the filter in place.
Screw the lens tube into the side of the cage cube nearest to the CCD camera.
Connect the camera to a computer and view the image on screen.
Direct the cage assembly at a distant object.
Slide the cage cube along the rails until an image appears in focus.
Lock down the cage cube at this location.
Insert the dichroic mirror into the holder and place it at 45° in the cage cube.
Screw the objective lens, via a RMS to SM1 thread adapter and an adjustable lens tube, into the face of the cage cube opposite the tube lens holder.
Mount an SMA connector into a cage plate and secure this plate on the rods, approximately at the working distance of the objective lens.
Attach an LED to a cage plate and slide it onto the end of the 2" rods.
Add a lens to a 0.5" lens tube such that when the tube is screwed into the side of the cage cube, it forms an image of the LED filling the back aperture of the objective lens.
Place the excitation filter in the 0.5" lens tube and secure it with a retaining ring.
Attach a SMA connector to a fiber-optic bundle.
Screw the SMA connectorized bundle into the SMA receptacle mounted on the cage rods.
Direct the distal end of the bundle towards a broadband light source and observe its image on the CCD camera.
Adjust the position of the objective lens by screwing it in or out until the fiber bundle image appears sharp and focused.
Ensure that the individual cores within the fiber bundle are clearly visible.
Attach a GRIN lens with the desired magnification and working distance to the distal tip of the fiber bundle.
Ensure the diameter of the GRIN lens exceeds that of the fiber bundle.
Mount the fiber bundle and GRIN lens on separate 3-axis manual positioning stages under a low power microscope or stereoscope for accurate alignment.
Place a drop of optical adhesive on either the lens or bundle face.
Bring the two components into contact using the manual positioners.
Expose the interface to UV light for the dose recommended by the manufacturer.
Apply the contrast agent to the cells or tissue to be imaged.
Incubate the cells with proflavine (0.01% w/v in PBS) for less than one minute and rinse thoroughly.
Place the fiber optic bundle in light contact with the sample to be imaged.
Mount the distal end of the fiber bundle in a secure fixture with manual positioning stages on XYZ axes for stability during imaging.
Imaging the proximal face of the fiber bundle onto the CCD camera without defocus.
Adjust the axial position of the objective lens relative to the bundle face to achieve optimal focus.
Configure the illumination optics for Kohler illumination.
Clean the proximal and distal faces of the fiber bundle using lens paper and isopropanol or standard fiber-optic cleaning tools.
Polish the face of the fiber bundle with 12-15 μm lapping paper for an initial coarse polish.
Perform a final polish on the fiber bundle face with 0.5-1.0 μm paper.
